summary:
ASTRAHEALTH is an AI-powered astronaut health monitoring software designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions. It collects and analyses important health indicators, including heart rate, blood oxygen levels, body temperature, sleep patterns, physical activity, stress levels and radiation exposure. The system uses data analysis and machine learning to identify unusual health patterns, detect potential risks and generate personalised health recommendations and alerts.

The software features an interactive dashboard, mental wellness assessment, radiation exposure tracker, health history graphs and an AI health assistant. It can also operate offline, allowing astronauts to access their health records even when communication with Earth is limited.

ASTRAHEALTH addresses the challenge of monitoring physical and psychological health in isolated space environments, where immediate medical assistance may not always be available. It is important because early identification of health changes can help astronauts take preventive action, maintain their well-being and improve safety during future long-duration missions to the Moon and Mars.
details:
ASTRAHEALTH – AI-Powered Astronaut Health Monitoring System

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

ASTRAHEALTH is a health monitoring software that we developed to help astronauts keep track of their physical and mental health during long space missions. As we know, living in space for months or even years can affect the human body in many ways. Problems like bone and muscle loss, radiation exposure, irregular sleep and mental stress can become serious challenges for astronauts.

Our software brings different health indicators together on one platform. It monitors information such as heart rate, blood oxygen levels (SpO₂), body temperature, sleep patterns, physical activity, stress levels and radiation exposure.

The collected data is displayed on a dashboard where astronauts can easily check their health status. The system also analyses changes in their readings over time. If it notices anything unusual, it generates an alert and suggests possible actions that the astronaut can take.

2. What benefits does it have?

The main benefit of ASTRAHEALTH is that it helps astronauts understand their health without having to depend on someone on Earth for every small update.

Some of its important benefits include:

  • Early Detection: Identifies unusual changes in health readings so astronauts can take action before a problem becomes more serious.
  • Physical Health Monitoring: Keeps track of important health indicators like heart rate, oxygen levels and body temperature.
  • Mental Health Support: Helps astronauts monitor their stress, mood and sleeping habits.
  • Radiation Tracking: Records radiation exposure and keeps track of cumulative exposure during the mission.
  • Personalised Suggestions: Provides recommendations based on the astronaut's health patterns.
  • Offline Access: Allows astronauts to access their stored health information even when there is no internet connection.
  • Health History: Maintains previous records so astronauts can understand how their health changes throughout the mission.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

Our main aim is to make long-duration space missions safer and help astronauts take better care of themselves.

During missions to the Moon or Mars, astronauts may face communication delays and limited access to medical assistance. In such situations, having a system that helps them understand their health becomes extremely important.

ASTRAHEALTH aims to give astronauts more control over their health by helping them notice unusual changes and take preventive action at the right time.

We also believe that this technology could have applications beyond space exploration. In the future, similar systems could be useful for people working in remote research stations, isolated locations and areas where immediate medical assistance is difficult to access.

4. What tools, programming languages and hardware did we use?

To develop ASTRAHEALTH, we planned a combination of software technologies and optional hardware components.

Software and Programming Languages:

  • Python – Used for processing health data and developing the backend.
  • HTML – Used to create the structure of the application.
  • CSS – Used to design the dashboard.
  • JavaScript – Used to make the application interactive.
  • Flask – Used for backend development.
  • SQLite – Used to store health records.
  • Chart.js – Used to display health information through graphs.
  • Scikit-learn – Used for machine learning and identifying unusual patterns.

Hardware (for sensor integration):

  • ESP32 – For collecting and transmitting sensor data.
  • MAX30102 – For measuring heart rate and blood oxygen levels.
  • DS18B20 – For temperature measurement.
  • MPU6050 – For monitoring movement and physical activity.

The software can initially work with simulated astronaut health data. Physical sensors can also be connected to make the system more practical and interactive.

5. How is the project creative and innovative?

What makes ASTRAHEALTH different from an ordinary health monitoring application is that it does not just show health readings. It also tries to understand how those readings change over time.

One of our main ideas is the Personal Health Digital Twin. Every astronaut has different health patterns, so instead of comparing everyone against the same standard, our system can establish an individual health baseline and compare new readings with it.

For example, if an astronaut usually has a resting heart rate of 70 BPM but it gradually increases over several days, the system can identify this change and generate an alert.

Another important feature is combined health analysis. Instead of checking every indicator separately, the system looks at multiple factors together. For example, reduced sleep, increasing stress and declining physical activity might indicate that an astronaut is experiencing difficulties.

We have also brought physical health monitoring, mental wellness tracking and radiation exposure monitoring together in a single platform. This makes ASTRAHEALTH more suitable for the different challenges astronauts face in space.

6. What factors did our team consider?

While planning this project, we considered the actual conditions astronauts experience during long-duration missions.

Some of the important factors were:

  • Space Environment: We considered the effects of radiation, microgravity, isolation and confinement on human health.
  • Reliability: The system should process and store health information consistently.
  • Easy to Use: Astronauts should be able to understand their health status without navigating complicated screens.
  • Offline Functionality: Since internet connectivity cannot always be guaranteed in space, the software should continue working without it.
  • Data Security: Personal health records should remain private and protected.
  • Personal Health Differences: Every astronaut has different health conditions, so the system should consider individual health patterns.
  • Future Expansion: We designed the concept so that additional sensors and monitoring features could be added later.
  • Medical Accuracy: The system should provide useful warnings and suggestions without pretending to replace professional medical advice.

Conclusion

Through ASTRAHEALTH, we wanted to work on a problem that will become increasingly important as humans travel farther into space. We believe that space exploration is not just about developing better rockets and spacecraft; it is also about making sure that the people travelling in them remain healthy and safe.

By bringing health monitoring, machine learning, radiation tracking and mental wellness assessment together, our project aims to give astronauts a better way to understand and manage their health during long missions.

Our vision is simple: As humanity travels farther into space, healthcare should travel with us.
